metadata.title: Applying Machine Learning and SHAP Method to Identify Key Influences on Middle-School Students’ Mathematics Literacy Performance

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: The study uses PISA 2022 microdata for six East Asian education systems (Hong Kong, Macao, Taipei, Singapore, Japan, and Korea) and constructs a student-level dataset with 34,495 cases after exclusions. The manuscript describes PISA’s two-stage sampling (PPS by school size, then random sampling of students within schools), but it does not report applying PISA sampling weights or any replicate-weight variance estimation in the ML training/evaluation. Because the models are standard scikit-learn-style regressors (MLR, SVR, DT, RF, XGBoost) and the paper does not mention weight-aware estimation, the analysis is treated as unweighted. Missing values are handled via KNN imputation after feature filtering, and the train/validation split is 80/20.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: Start from PISA 2022 data for the six East Asian education systems (Hong Kong, Macao, Taipei, Singapore, Japan, Korea) with 34,968 students. Exclude students with missing rate >70%, leaving 34,495 students. Select 151 candidate predictors (77 student, 17 household, 57 school); drop predictors with missing rate >70%, retaining 124. Exclude variables that are entirely missing for each country/region (e.g., well-being questionnaire not administered in Japan, Korea, Singapore, Taipei), reducing to 78 variables. Remove variables with moderate/strong multicollinearity by excluding six correlated variables (ICTWKDY, HOMEPOS, PAREDINT, ICTAVSCH, ICTAVHOM, MCLSIZE), leaving 72 predictors. Impute remaining missing values using KNN with K=8. Use PV1MATH as the outcome and split the final dataset into training (80%) and validation (20%) sets.

main_findings.dataset_used: PISA 2022 Mathematics literacy (PV1MATH), six East Asian education systems (Hong Kong, Macao, Taipei, Singapore, Japan, Korea)
main_findings.performance_metrics: XGBoost (best): MSE=4344.98, RMSE=65.92, MAE=51.72, MAPE=10.21%, R2=0.60, PCC=0.77 (validation set). Other models: MLR R2=0.49, SVR R2=0.58, DT R2=0.32, RF R2=0.54.
main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using PISA 2022 Mathematics literacy (PV1MATH) the study leveraged math self-efficacy (MATHEFF), expected occupational status (BSMJ), ESCS, ICT weekend leisure frequency (ICTWKEND), and math anxiety (ANXMAT) to predict mathematics literacy, finding that XGBoost achieved the highest validation performance (R2=0.60; PCC=0.77) and that MATHEFF was the strongest positive contributor while ANXMAT and ICTWKEND were negative contributors via SHAP. This indicates that strengthening students’ mathematics self-efficacy and reducing math anxiety—while discouraging excessive weekend ICT leisure—may be promising targets for interventions, though the SHAP-based importance is predictive rather than causal and the paper does not report survey-weighted estimation.

data.outcome_summary: The study analyzes PISA 2022 mathematics literacy for 15-year-old students from six East Asian education systems (Hong Kong, Macao, Taipei, Singapore, Japan, Korea), using PV1MATH as the outcome. After excluding students with >70% missingness and filtering predictors with >70% missingness, the final analytic dataset contains 34,495 students and 72 features; missing values are imputed using KNN (K=8). Five regression ML models (MLR, SVR, DT, RF, XGBoost) are tuned via GridSearchCV with 5-fold cross-validation and evaluated on an 80/20 train/validation split using MSE, RMSE, MAE, MAPE, R2, and Pearson correlation. XGBoost performs best on the validation set (R2=0.60; PCC=0.77; MAPE=10.21%). SHAP global explanations identify 15 key predictors, with math self-efficacy (MATHEFF) the largest positive contributor and math anxiety (ANXMAT) and ICT weekend leisure (ICTWKEND) negative; however, SHAP is not causal and the manuscript does not report applying PISA sampling weights.
